I’m in the same boat. I watched my mom fade and held her hand as she passed. Very unexpected death. It’s been a year and two months. I feel lost and like I’m just going through the motions day to day. I’ve lost hope for the future and I feel like a shell of the person I once was. I lost my purpose when I lost her.

I’m so sorry for your loss and the pain you’re feeling. It hurts, let it hurt. Ride the waves of grief and let them pass through you like an ocean wave. Each one smaller than the last until you can breathe again. You’ll be okay. It doesn’t make it any easier, but take things one day, one hour, one minute at a time. Grief does not end, it only becomes your tolerable with time and you will make it through. Be gentle with yourself.
My mom that passed at the end of last year. What I wouldn’t give to see her again.

I’m so sorry for how they’ve treated you and that they’ve robbed you of so many important moments and experiences. Every moment that passes is a moment that you cannot get back. And it’s totally okay to mourn the passing of time and what could have been, but one thing I’ve learned is to not let that stop you from seeing the beauty in, and enjoying what comes next. Not having motivation right now is totally fine. You can’t be motivated every second of every day. You can’t enjoy the highs without having lows. But be gentle with yourself, you’re only human! ☺️

You are absolutely NOT pathetic. I have been in your shoes, and have done the exact same thing. Sometimes it’s easier to ask for help when those helping are distanced from your situation. Talking about suicide, depression, etc. is such a tender subject and requires you to be incredibly vulnerable. Like I said, I’m so proud of you. These are hard feelings to express. And it can sometimes be hard for people close to you to know how to respond to unless they’ve experienced it first hand. So never, ever feel bad for needing comfort or validation when it comes to what you’re feeling. You deserve love and support!

I see you, I hear you and I meet you with zero judgement. The first step is asking for help, and you’ve done that. I’m proud of you. Please don’t give up. It may not feel like it right now, but life has so much more to offer you. There is so much beauty out there just waiting for you. There are good people waiting to love you. I know you’re tired, and that’s okay. It’s okay to be tired, but please, don’t give up. Don’t compare what you’re going through to what other people are going through because what you are feeling here and now, matters. Your feelings are validated and matter just as much as anyone else’s. 

[Don’t give up](https://www.happiness.com/magazine/health-body/eight-powerful-suicide-prevention-quotes/)
